by President of the United States
Abolishing Malagi (Malahi) Island Military Reservation, Laguna de Bay, Luzon, Philippine Islands

Executive Order 405-B

→

sister projects: Wikidata item

more info.

See unnumbered Executive Order of November 6, 1902.

Signed by President Theodore Roosevelt Thursday, February 1, 1906

General Orders, No. 28, War Dept., February 7, 1906

619471Executive Order 405-A — Abolishing Malagi (Malahi) Island Military Reservation, Laguna de Bay, Luzon, Philippine Islands1906President of the United States

The military reservation of Malagi (Malahi) Island, situated at the south end of Talim Island, in Laguna de Bay, Luzon, Philippine Islands, made by Executive Order of November 6, 1902 (G. O., No. 121, Headquarters of the Army, A. G. O., November 24, 1902), having become useless for military purposes, is hereby restored to the control of the government of the Philippine Islands to be administered for the benefit of the inhabitants thereof.

Theodore Roosevelt.

The White House, February 1, 1906.

This work is in the public domain in the United States because it is a work of the United States federal government (see 17 U.S.C. 105).

# IR1912:p223:1: order signed by Roosevelt, 1906-01-31 (WDTD RIVER OR SHOSHONE RESERVATION, Wyoming); matched to EO:404B in the WPA numbered list (exact_date)
# Source: Executive Orders Relating to Indian Reservations, from May 14, 1855, to July 1, 1912 (Washington: Government Printing Office, 1912); Cornell University Library copy (Huntington Free Library Native American Collection), scanned by the Internet Archive (cu31924097621753); PDF generated by HathiTrust, handle 2027/coo1.ark:/13960/t9q254654
# PDF: releases/source_books/Executive_Orders_Relating_to_Indian_Reservations_1855-1912_coo1.ark-13960-t9q254654.pdf sha256 33e2e6067048f26ef5fbefede181a9325d3f1e3fc4b085ffa636f20edcbe8192
# PDF pages 236-236; printed pages 223-223; date from header; confidence high
# Text: OCR text layer of the scan (pypdf 6.20.1 extract_text(), NUL characters removed; the layer is the Internet Archive's OCR), running heads and page numbers removed. Not human-verified. Body sha256 2ff0a8dccc459228204f613e8d01d00302321b22ba47fc770756d3f593a40a55

The White House, January 31, 1906.
A new survey having been made by First Lieutenant James Hus-
ton, lenth Cavalry, of the military reservation of Fort Washakie.
Wyommg, reserved by Executive order of May 21, 1887 (G. O. No.37, Headquarters of the Army, A. G. O., May 26, 1887), as deter-mmed from the old corner monuments, except that Corner II has
been moved so as to exclude the part of the reservation encroached
upon in the construction of buildings pertaining to the Indian school,the reservation as made by said Executive order of May 21, 1887, is
hereby modified, in accordance with said new survey, so as to includeall lands, and those only, within metes and bounds described as
follows :
Commencing at a point 3,861 feet S. 2° 30' E. of the flagstaff ofFort Washakie, Wyoming, and running thence N. 75° 30' E. 11,890
feet to Corner II; thence N. 26° 15' W. 7,060 feet to Corner III;
thence S. 83° 15' W. 13,125 feet to Comer IV; thence S. 23° 00' W.
6,435 feet to Corner V; thence N. 87° 45' E. 3,234 feet to Corner VI:
thence S. 61° 30' E. 4,450 feet to Comer I, the place of begijining.
All bearings are true.
This modification is made subject to the proviso in said Executive
order of May 21, 1887, that—
_
" The use and occupancy of the land in question be subject to such
right, title, and interest as the Indians have in and to the same, and
that it be vacated whenever the interest of the Indians shall require
it,upon notice to that effect to the Secretary of War."
T. Roosevelt.
